mainTopic: Testing רבה's rule (what cannot happen one after another cannot happen at once), and the argument between אביי and רבא about קידושין שאין מסורין לביאה
overview: The גמרא keeps testing רבה's rule that anything which cannot take effect one after another cannot take effect all at once either. It brings three cases that seem to break the rule. The first is someone who separates too much מעשר; regular מעשר can apply to half of each grain. The second is two animals called 'tenth' in מעשר בהמה; that can take effect on several animals through a mistake. The third is a תודה brought with eighty loaves. רבי יהושע בן לוי explains that the argument there is about what the owner meant, not about רבה's rule. The גמרא then asks why רבא used רבה's rule at all, and answers that he was speaking on רמי בר חמא's terms. Next it lays out the argument between אביי and רבא about a קידושין that can never lead to permitted living together. It tests רבא's view against our משנה, and רבא answers back from the end of the same משנה about five women. The discussion of that case continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Challenge from someone who separates too much tithe
steps.stepSummary: A source teaches that if someone separates too much מעשר, his produce is still fixed. That seems to contradict רבה's rule, since you cannot separate two tenths one after the other.
steps.simpleTranslation: If someone separates more than the proper tithe, his produce is fixed but his tithes are ruined. Why should the produce be fixed? We should apply the rule: whatever cannot happen one after another cannot happen at once either.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes a ruling about someone who separates too much מעשר and uses it to attack רבה's principle.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Once one tenth is separated, a second tenth cannot become מעשר afterward. So by רבה's rule, separating two tenths at once should fail completely, and the produce should stay untithed. Yet the ruling says the produce is fixed, which means the separation worked.

keyTerms.meaning: One who separates more than the proper amount of tithe
Fixed, meaning properly tithed and allowed to eat
Ruined, meaning the status is unclear and the food cannot be used normally
All at once, at the same time

steps.confusionAlert: 'His produce is fixed' refers to the rest of the produce he kept. Only the oversized tithe portion is 'ruined.'

phrases.english: One who separates too much tithe —
his produce is fixed
and his tithes are ruined.
But why? Let us say:
anything that cannot take effect one after another
cannot take effect even all at once.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the earlier testing of רבה's principle with a new source.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבה's principle that what cannot happen in sequence cannot happen all at once
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Two tenths cannot be separated one after another, so by the principle a double separation should fail. Yet the produce is considered tithed.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Separating too much tithe fixes the produce but ruins the tithe portion.

steps.title: Tithe can take effect on half a grain
steps.stepSummary: רבה answers that מעשר is different because it can apply to part of a grain. The double portion becomes half-tithe in every grain.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: tithe is different, because it works on halves. If someone says 'Let half of this wheat grain become holy,' it becomes holy.
steps.whatsHappening: רבה answers the challenge by showing that the case of מעשר does not really break his rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since מעשר can apply to half a grain, the two tenths do not need to be two separate tenths. Each grain in that portion is simply half tithe and half not, so exactly one tenth of the produce becomes מעשר. That is why the produce is fixed, and the tithe portion is ruined because nobody can tell which half of each grain is holy.

keyTerms.meaning: In halves, taking effect on part of an item

phrases.english: He said to him: Tithe is different,
since it can take effect in halves,
for if one said:
'Let half of the wheat grain become holy,' it becomes holy.

steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinguishing the case: מעשר has a special feature that avoids the principle
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The double separation looked like two whole tenths taking effect together, which the principle should block.
steps.terutzMaskana: It is really one tenth spread out as half of every grain, so the principle never comes into play.

steps.title: Challenge from two animals called 'tenth'
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא raises מעשר בהמה, which cannot work in halves or one after another. Yet רבא rules that when two animals are called 'tenth' together, holiness does take effect.
steps.simpleTranslation: But what about animal tithe, which cannot apply in halves or one after another? And רבא said: if two animals came out together as the tenth and he called them both 'tenth,' the tenth and the eleventh are mixed up with each other.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new case where רבה's answer about halves cannot help, and uses it to challenge his rule again.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Half an animal cannot become מעשר, and after the tenth animal is named, another animal cannot become מעשר. By רבה's rule, calling two animals 'tenth' at once should fail completely. But רבא says the two animals are 'mixed up,' which shows that holiness did take effect.

keyTerms.meaning: Animal tithe: every tenth animal is set aside as holy
There is not, it does not apply
Mixed up, it is unknown which is which

steps.confusionAlert: Don't confuse רבה, whose principle is being tested, with רבא, whose ruling is being quoted against it.

phrases.english: But there is animal tithe,
which does not take effect in halves,
and does not take effect one after another.
And רבא said:
If two came out together as the tenth,
phrases.notes: The animals pass through a gate one by one to be counted. Here two squeezed out together at the tenth spot.

phrases.english: and he called them 'tenth,'
the tenth and the eleventh
are mixed up with each other.
phrases.notes: One of them is the tithe animal and the other is a שלמים, but we can't tell which is which.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new challenge chosen so that the 'halves' answer of step 2 cannot work.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבה's principle, and the limits of his answer in step 2
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Animal tithe cannot apply in halves or in sequence. By the principle, naming two animals at once should fail, yet רבא treats holiness as having taken effect.

steps.title: Animal tithe can take effect through a mistake
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that מעשר בהמה is different, because by mistake more than one animal can become holy one after another.
steps.simpleTranslation: Animal tithe is different, because it can take effect through a mistake.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends רבה's rule by showing that animal tithe can in fact take effect on more than one animal in sequence, in a case of error.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rule only blocks things that can never happen one after another. Since mistaken naming can make several animals holy in sequence, animal tithe does have a 'one after another' form, so naming two at once can also work.

phrases.english: Animal tithe is different,
since it can take effect through a mistake.

steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinguishing the case: animal tithe can work in sequence through error
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Animal tithe seemed to have no way to take effect one after another, so naming two together should fail.
steps.terutzMaskana: Through a mistake it can take effect one after another, so naming two at once also works and the principle is not broken.

steps.title: Proof: three mistakenly named animals are all holy
steps.stepSummary: A משנה shows that when the ninth, tenth and eleventh animals are mixed up in naming, all three become holy.
steps.simpleTranslation: As we learned in a משנה: if he called the ninth 'tenth,' the tenth 'ninth,' and the eleventh 'tenth,' all three are holy.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a משנה to prove that animal tithe can take effect on several animals through a mistake.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ninth is holy because he called it 'tenth.' The tenth is holy because it really is the tenth. The eleventh is holy because he called it 'tenth.' So several animals became holy one after another, which supports the answer in step 4.
steps.whatToRemember: So far, רבה's rule (what cannot happen one after another cannot happen all at once) survives both challenges. Regular מעשר works in halves, and מעשר בהמה can work in sequence through a mistake, so neither case truly breaks the rule. The next step brings one more challenge, from the loaves of a תודה.

phrases.english: As we learned in a משנה:
If he called the ninth 'tenth,'
and the tenth 'ninth,'
and the eleventh 'tenth' —
all three of them are holy.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supplies the source for the claim in step 4.
steps.raayaObject: That animal tithe can take effect on more than one animal through a mistake
steps.raayaSupportSource: A משנה about mistakenly naming the ninth, tenth and eleventh animals

steps.title: The thanks-offering with eighty loaves
steps.stepSummary: The loaves of a תודה cannot become holy by mistake or one after another. Yet חזקיה says that when a תודה is slaughtered with eighty loaves, forty of them become holy. That seems to go against רבה's rule.
steps.simpleTranslation: Look at the תודה. Its loaves don't become holy by mistake, and they also don't become holy one set after another. And yet it was said: if a תודה was slaughtered with eighty loaves, חזקיה says forty out of the eighty become holy, and רבי יוחנן says forty out of the eighty do not become holy.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new challenge to רבה's rule, using the loaves of a תודה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A תודה needs forty loaves. The loaves cannot become holy by mistake, and two sets cannot become holy one after the other, so by רבה's rule eighty loaves brought together should not work at all. But חזקיה says forty of the eighty do become holy, which seems to break רבה's rule.

keyTerms.meaning: A thanks-offering, which is brought together with forty loaves

steps.confusionAlert: Only חזקיה's view causes the problem. רבי יוחנן's view (none become holy) fits רבה's rule just fine.

phrases.english: There is the thanks-offering,
phrases.notes: He means the forty loaves that come with the תודה.

phrases.english: which does not take effect by mistake,
and also does not take effect one after another,
and it was stated:
A thanks-offering that was slaughtered with eighty loaves,
phrases.notes: That is double the forty loaves a תודה needs.

phrases.english: חזקיה said:
Forty out of the eighty become holy for it.
And רבי יוחנן said:

phrases.aramaic: לָא קָדְשִׁי לַהּ אַרְבָּעִים מִתּוֹךְ שְׁמוֹנִים.
phrases.english: Forty out of the eighty do not become holy for it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After מעשר בהמה was explained as a special case, the גמרא brings another case that seems to break רבה's rule.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבה's rule that what cannot take effect one after another cannot take effect all at once
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: תודה loaves fail both tests (no mistake, no one-after-another), yet חזקיה rules forty of eighty become holy together.

steps.title: Everyone agrees when the owner spells it out
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהושע בן לוי says both sides agree: if the owner said 'let forty of the eighty be holy,' they are holy; if he said 'only if all eighty are holy,' none are.
steps.simpleTranslation: Wasn't it said about this argument: רבי יהושע בן לוי said, everyone agrees that if he said 'let forty out of the eighty become holy,' they become holy. If he said 'forty should not become holy unless eighty become holy,' they do not become holy.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the challenge by quoting רבי יהושע בן לוי, who shows the argument is not really about רבה's rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: When the owner clearly says what he wants, nobody argues. So the argument between חזקיה and רבי יוחנן is not about whether two sets can become holy together. It must be about something else, which the next step explains.

phrases.english: Wasn't it stated about this:
רבי יהושע בן לוי said:
Everyone agrees
that wherever he said:
'Let forty out of the eighty become holy for it' —
they become holy;
'Forty should not become holy
unless eighty become holy' —
they do not become holy.

steps.triggerLanguage: לָאו אִיתְּמַר עֲלַהּ, אָמַר רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ בֶּן לֵוִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 6 by showing the argument is not about רבה's rule.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the idea that חזקיה and רבי יוחנן argue about רבה's rule
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The challenge assumed the argument is about holiness taking effect together; really it depends on what the owner meant.

steps.title: The real argument: backup or one big offering
steps.stepSummary: They only argue when the owner said nothing specific. חזקיה thinks he brought the extra forty as backup, so forty are holy. רבי יוחנן thinks he wanted one big offering of eighty, so none are holy.
steps.simpleTranslation: They only argued when he didn't say anything specific. One master holds: he means the extra loaves as backup. And the other master holds: he means to bring a big offering.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes the answer by explaining what חזקיה and רבי יוחנן actually argue about.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For חזקיה, the owner only wanted forty loaves to be holy and the rest were spare, so only one set ever became holy. For רבי יוחנן, he wanted all eighty as one offering, which is too many, so nothing becomes holy. Either way, רבה's rule is never broken.

keyTerms.meaning: As a backup, as a guarantee

steps.whatToRemember: The תודה argument is about the owner's intention, not about holiness taking effect together, so רבה's rule still stands.

phrases.english: They only argued when he said nothing specific.
One master holds:
He means the extra loaves as backup.
And the other master holds:
He means to bring a big offering.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues רבי יהושע בן לוי's words and explains the real argument.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Redefining the argument as a question of the owner's intention
steps.terutzHavaAmina: חזקיה holds that two sets of loaves can partly become holy at once, against רבה.
steps.terutzMaskana: חזקיה holds the owner meant only forty to be holy from the start, so there is no clash with רבה's rule.

steps.title: Why did רבא need רבה's rule?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא goes back to רבא, who explained our משנה using רבה's rule. Why not use רבא's own rule that a קידושין which can never lead to living together does not take effect?
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבא, why does he need to explain it like רבה? Let him get it from a different reason: these are a קידושין that cannot lead to living together.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא leaves the testing of רבה's rule and goes back to רבא's explanation of the משנה, asking why he chose that path.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier, רבא explained the משנה using רבה's rule. But רבא has his own rule: a קידושין where the couple could never be allowed to live together does not work. Since the man could not be married to both related women, that rule alone should be enough to explain why neither is מקודשת.

keyTerms.meaning: To explain, to give an answer
Let him get it from (a different reason)
Able to lead to living together as husband and wife

phrases.english: And רבא, why does he need
to explain it like רבה?
Let him get it from a different reason:
These are a קידושין that cannot lead to living together.
phrases.notes: He could never live with both women, since each is a relative of the other, so the קידושין should not work anyway.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After defending רבה's rule, the גמרא returns to רבא, who used that rule, and questions why he needed it.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבא's choice to explain the משנה using רבה's rule
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבא already holds that קידושין שאין מסורין לביאה does not take effect, which would explain the משנה more simply.

steps.title: רבא was speaking on רמי בר חמא's terms
steps.stepSummary: רבא used רבה's rule only because he was answering inside רמי בר חמא's way of thinking.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said it according to the words of רמי בר חמא.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question from step 9. רבא explained the משנה with רבה's rule only because he was responding to רמי בר חמא on רמי בר חמא's own terms.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא was not giving his own personal reason for the משנה. He was correcting רמי בר חמא's explanation within the framework רמי בר חמא was already using. So the fact that רבא used רבה's rule does not mean he gave up his own rule.

keyTerms.meaning: according to his words, meaning according to his way of thinking

phrases.english: He was speaking according to the words of רמי בר חמא.
phrases.notes: In other words, רבא was answering רמי בר חמא on his own terms, not giving his own main reason.

steps.terutzResolutionType: Contextual answer: the statement was made within another person's framework.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Since רבא used רבה's rule, it seemed he did not rely on his own rule about betrothal that cannot lead to living together.
steps.terutzMaskana: רבא was correcting רמי בר חמא on his own terms. His own rule still stands.

steps.title: אביי and רבא argue about betrothal that can never lead to permitted living together
steps.stepSummary: אביי says such a betrothal works. רבא says it does not, and he learns this from the פסוק 'כי יקח איש אשה ובעלה'.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was stated: about a betrothal that is not open to permitted living together, אביי says it is a betrothal and רבא says it is not. רבא said: בר אהינא explained it to me from the פסוק 'When a man takes a woman and lives with her.' A betrothal that can lead to living together is a betrothal. One that cannot lead to living together is not a betrothal.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now presents, in full, the argument between אביי and רבא about a קידושין that can never lead to permitted living together. רבא also gives the source for his view.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אביי holds that a ban on living together does not undo the betrothal itself. רבא reads the פסוק as tying קידושין to permitted living together ('takes' and then 'lives with her'). So a betrothal that can never lead to permitted living together does not take effect at all.

keyTerms.meaning: a betrothal that can never lead to permitted living together
the חכם who taught רבא this source

steps.whyThisMatters: This argument is the base for the challenges that follow, and the next lines test each side against the משנה.

phrases.english: It was stated: a betrothal that is not open to permitted living together,
אביי says: it is a betrothal.
רבא says: it is not a betrothal.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רָבָא: בַּר אֲהִינָא אַסְבְּרַהּ לִי:
phrases.english: רבא said: בר אהינא explained it to me:
"When a man takes a woman and lives with her",
a betrothal that is open to living together is a betrothal,

phrases.aramaic: קִידּוּשִׁין שֶׁאֵין מְסוּרִין לְבִיאָה – לָא הָווּ קִידּוּשִׁין.
phrases.english: a betrothal that is not open to living together is not a betrothal.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Step 9 mentioned רבא's rule. Now the גמרא lays out the full dispute and its source.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: אביי: a betrothal that cannot lead to permitted living together is valid. רבא: it is not valid, based on 'כי יקח איש אשה ובעלה'.

steps.title: Challenge to רבא: betrothing one unnamed woman of a related pair works
steps.stepSummary: The משנה implies that betrothing 'one of' a woman and her daughter or sister works, even though he can never live with either one. That seems to refute רבא.
steps.simpleTranslation: We learned: one who betroths a woman and her daughter, or a woman and her sister, together: they are not betrothed. This implies that if he betroths one of a woman and her daughter, or one of a woman and her sister, she is betrothed. But why? This is a betrothal that cannot lead to living together! This is a refutation of רבא!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רבא from our משנה. It reads an implication out of the משנה that seems to go against him.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If he betroths 'one of the two' without saying which one, he can never live with either woman. Each might be the relative of his real wife. That is exactly a betrothal that cannot lead to living together, yet the משנה implies it works. That fits אביי and seems to break רבא's rule.

keyTerms.meaning: this implies, used to draw an inference from the wording

steps.confusionAlert: The משנה itself only says that betrothing both together fails. The case of 'one of them' is an inference the גמרא draws from the wording. It is not written openly.

phrases.english: We learned: one who betroths a woman and her daughter
or a woman and her sister together,
they are not betrothed.
This implies: one of a woman and her daughter,
or of a woman and her sister, is betrothed.
But why?
It is a betrothal that is not open to living together!
A refutation of רבא!

steps.triggerLanguage: תְּנַן: הַמְקַדֵּשׁ אִשָּׁה וּבִתָּהּ אוֹ אִשָּׁה וַאֲחוֹתָהּ כְּאַחַת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tests רבא's view from step 11 against the משנה.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבא's rule that a betrothal that cannot lead to living together does not take effect.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The משנה implies that betrothing an unspecified one of two related women works, even though he can never live with either. That goes against רבא.

steps.title: רבא answers back from the end of the same משנה
steps.stepSummary: רבא replies that the end of the משנה, about five women including two sisters, makes trouble for אביי too.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא can say to you: and according to your reasoning, say the end of the משנה: It happened with five women, and among them were two sisters. A man gathered a basket of figs, which were theirs and were Sabbatical-year produce, and said: 'You are all betrothed to me with this basket.' And the חכמים said: the sisters are not betrothed. This implies: it is the sisters who are not betrothed, but the unrelated women are betrothed.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא pushes back by quoting the next part of the same משנה. The גמרא is setting up a difficulty for אביי's side, and the point will be finished in the coming lines.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא's move is 'ולטעמיך', meaning your own view has a problem here too. In this case, too, there are sisters he can never marry both of, and the משנה says the sisters are not betrothed while the others are. רבא will use this ruling to show that the משנה does not simply support אביי, which weakens the refutation from step 12.

keyTerms.meaning: he can say to you, introducing a possible reply
and according to your own reasoning
the later part of a משנה
the Sabbatical year and its produce
unrelated women, here the ones who are not the sisters

phrases.english: רבא can say to you: and according to your reasoning,
say the end of the משנה:
An incident with five women,
and among them were two sisters,
and a man gathered a basket of figs,
and it was theirs,
and it was Sabbatical-year produce,
and he said: "You are all betrothed to me
with this basket."
And the חכמים said: the sisters are not betrothed.
It is the sisters who are not betrothed,
but the unrelated women are betrothed.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר לָךְ רָבָא: וּלְטַעְמָיךְ, אֵימָא סֵיפָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Defends רבא against step 12 by turning the משנה back on אביי.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The claim that the משנה clearly refutes רבא.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The same משנה, in its end part, also raises a difficulty for אביי's view, so it cannot be used one-sidedly against רבא.

steps.title: What exactly did he say to the five women?
steps.stepSummary: רבא asks what the case of the five women (including two sisters) in the end of the משנה actually looks like.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up the next move. It asks how the man worded his betrothal to the five women, so the options can be tested one at a time.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In Step 13, רבא said the end of the משנה makes trouble for אביי too. To prove that, he first has to pin down the exact wording the man used. Each possible wording will be checked against the משנה's ruling that the sisters are not betrothed but the other women are.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the case? How exactly did it happen?

phrases.english: What are the circumstances?
phrases.notes: He means the end of the משנה: five women, two of them sisters, and one gift given to all of them.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts unpacking רבא's claim from Step 13 that the end of the משנה is difficult for אביי.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The exact wording the man used when he betrothed the five women.

steps.title: If he said 'all of you,' it is like 'you and the donkey'
steps.stepSummary: If he said 'all of you are betrothed,' that is like 'let you and the donkey acquire.' In that kind of case nothing is acquired, so the other women should not be betrothed either.
steps.simpleTranslation: If you say he said 'all of you' are betrothed to me, that is like saying 'let you and the donkey acquire.' And with 'you and the donkey,' the person does not acquire.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא tests the first option, that the man said 'all of you.' He rejects it, because then the משנה's ruling that the other women are betrothed would not make sense.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A donkey cannot acquire anything. If someone says 'you and the donkey acquire this,' he has tied the two together, so the person does not acquire either. Here the sisters cannot be betrothed together, so they are like the donkey. That means the other women should not be betrothed either, but the משנה says they are. So the case in the end of the משנה cannot be one where he said 'all of you.' The גמרא looks for a different wording on the next amud.

keyTerms.meaning: If you say (offers an option that will be rejected)
Let you and the donkey acquire. A gift given jointly to someone who can acquire and something that cannot.

steps.confusionAlert: The donkey is not part of the case of the women. It is only a comparison. The sisters, who cannot be betrothed together, play the role of the donkey.

phrases.english: If you say that he said: "All of you"
phrases.notes: He means he told the five women, 'All of you are betrothed to me.'

phrases.english: it is like "Let you and the donkey acquire,"
phrases.notes: The two sisters, who can't be betrothed together, are like the donkey, who can't acquire anything.

phrases.english: and with "you and the donkey," he does not acquire.

steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects reading the end of the משנה as a case where he said 'all of you.'
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: With 'all of you,' the sisters are like the donkey in 'you and the donkey,' so no one would acquire. That clashes with the משנה's ruling that the other women are betrothed.
